topic: OpenAI (Sora) and Google (Veo, Flow, Genie, Gemini Omni), 2024 through 2026-09-29
method_notes: All pages were fetched from the Higgsfield sandbox (open internet). Every quote was checked programmatically against the fetched page text (whitespace-normalised, HTML entities decoded) and none exceeds 25 words. OpenAI marketing pages (openai.com, help.openai.com) return 403 from the sandbox, so they are cited as Wayback Machine id_ captures with the exact capture timestamp in the URL; OpenAI API docs (developers.openai.com) and all Google pages were fetched live. One claim (Omni Flash launch date) quotes page metadata rather than visible text. The Veo 3 tech report PDF carries no date inside; 2025-05-27 is its HTTP Last-Modified header. Model version names are spelled as each developer writes them.

corrections_to_common_beliefs: Sora was NOT publicly released in February 2024. The 15 Feb 2024 event was a research preview shown to red teamers and a few artists, designers and filmmakers. The public release came on 9 Dec 2024 as a different, faster model called Sora Turbo, with clips capped at 20 seconds and 1080p, not the 'minute' shown in February.

Sora is now a past-tense story. OpenAI discontinued the Sora web and app on 26 April 2026 (announced 24 March 2026) and shut down the Sora 2 API on 24 September 2026; its own docs say no one-to-one replacement API exists. Sora 1 left the U.S. on 13 March 2026. Any line calling Sora 2 the current state of the art, or an OpenAI product you can use today, is wrong.

Sora 2 (30 Sep 2025) did not bring native audio ahead of Google: Veo 3 shipped generated dialogue, sound effects and ambience on 20 May 2025, about four months earlier. (Other developers are outside the scope of this file.)

Veo 2's December 2024 headline ('up to 4K', 'minutes in length') is a capability claim, not what users got. The Gemini API spec table in April 2025 lists 5-8 second clips at 720p and 24 fps. Similarly Veo 1's 'beyond a minute at 1080p' (May 2024) was shown only to select creators in a private preview.

Veo 3.1 (15 Oct 2025) is no longer Google's newest video model. Gemini Omni Flash launched on 19 May 2026 and Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash reached general availability on 27 Aug 2026 (API ID gemini-omni-1.1-flash). Google's Gemini app page says Omni replaces Veo in the app, and the API docs make Omni Flash the default. Veo 3.1 remains available for specific features (scene extension, last-frame control) and no 'Veo 4' has been announced.

'Gemini Omni' is real and verified in Google primary sources (blog.google, Gemini API docs and changelog, DeepMind model card), not a leak or rumour. Use the exact strings 'Gemini Omni Flash' (launch) and 'Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash' (August 2026).

Omni's 1080p and 4K outputs are generated by upscaling, and a single generation is 3-10 seconds; longer clips come from extension (10-second steps, 40 seconds cumulative per the Aug 2026 developer post). Google's January 2026 post likewise describes Veo 3.1's 1080p and 4K options as upscaling, available only in Flow, the Gemini API and Vertex AI. Do not claim native 4K generation.

Longer durations come from extension and stitching, not from single long generations: Sora API videos reach their 120-second maximum only by repeated extensions (each adds up to 20 seconds, up to six times), Veo 3.1's 8-second clips reach 148 seconds only by chaining extensions, and Omni 1.1 reaches 40 seconds by 10-second extension steps.

Vertical 9:16 output dates: Sora's technical report described native 1080x1920 sampling as a capability in Feb 2024 (the public Sora product offered vertical from Dec 2024); Veo 3 and Veo 3 Fast got a 9:16 option in the Gemini API on 8 Sep 2025; Veo 3.1 Ingredients to Video got what Google calls native vertical output on 13 Jan 2026.

Sora's public clips were watermarked: a visible moving watermark plus C2PA metadata at the Sora app launch. Any Sora 2 excerpt would need that watermark left in place, and per OpenAI's own pages the app, web and API are all discontinued, so no new Sora 2 footage can be generated.

Google's Genie 3 and Project Genie are interactive world models (real time, 720p, consistent for a few minutes, 60-second worlds in the prototype), not clip generators. Present them as 'moving worlds', not as video-model milestones.
